video_script.title: Gil Pepperday Keeps the Coolers Running
video_script.hook: Third-generation mortuary operator in Phoenix describes his role as "mostly just keeping the coolers running" as heat seasons stretch longer into fall.
body_slides: Three generations. Same business. Same ritual.
Twice he offers water before you sit.
video_script.voiceover_text: Gil Pepperday runs a Phoenix funeral home founded by his grandfather in 1974. He keeps the office at 68 degrees and offers visitors water twice before they sit down. Three generations. Same business. Same ritual. Twice he offers water before you sit. The coolers never stop running. Some family legacies grow heavier each summer. video_script.title: The Moratorium That Came Too Late
video_script.hook: A security guard barricaded himself inside while fishers tried to break down the door.
body_slides: They called it a two-year pause.
The fishers believed the minister's timeline.
But the Grand Banks had already decided.
video_script.voiceover_text: A security guard jammed a chair through door handles to keep angry fishers out. The year was 1992. They called it a two-year pause. The fishers believed the minister's timeline. But the Grand Banks had already decided. Thirty-two years later, the cod still haven't returned. Follow for more stories like this at The Docket.
